questions.question: Which of these is a discrete quantity?
options: The temperature of a CPU over an hour
The number of compile errors in a file
The position of a drone along a flight path
questions.explanation: Error counts come in separate whole pieces — there is no 2.5th error. The others vary smoothly over a range.

questions.question: A continuous quantity is best described as one that…
options: can only be counted with a computer
takes any value in a range, with no gaps
questions.explanation: Discrete values are separated into individual pieces; continuous ones vary smoothly across intervals.

questions.question: Which sentence describes a relationship between discrete objects rather than a smooth quantity?
options: Course A conflicts with course B in the schedule
The server's load rose 12% this hour
questions.explanation: Conflicts are yes/no relations between objects — exactly the structure discrete math models.

questions.question: Why is a computer naturally suited to discrete mathematics?
options: It computes faster than any calculator
It stores a finite number of bits and takes discrete steps
questions.explanation: A machine made of finitely many bits doing finitely many steps per second is itself a discrete object.

questions.question: Which claim about programs could running millions of tests never fully settle?
options: The parser crashes on this specific input file
The average latency yesterday was under 200 ms
This function never loops forever, for any input
The login page renders in under a second on this phone
questions.explanation: Forever-for-any-input quantifies over infinitely many cases; tests sample finitely many. It needs a proof.

questions.question: How many subsets does a set with n elements have?
questions.explanation: Each element is either in or out — 2 independent choices per element, giving 2ⁿ. The lesson proves this by a bijection with bit strings.

questions.question: The 2ⁿ-subsets proof works by…
options: induction on the size of the set
listing all subsets and counting them
pairing each subset with an n-bit string, one-to-one
measuring how fast the count grows
questions.explanation: A bijection between subsets and bit strings transfers the count; the bit strings are counted by the product rule.

questions.question: A bijection between two collections tells you…
options: they have exactly the same size
one is finite and the other is not
questions.explanation: A one-to-one pairing uses every element exactly once on each side, so the counts must agree.

questions.question: You can verify a claim about ALL natural numbers by brute force because…
options: you cannot — finite checks never cover an infinite domain
questions.explanation: Enumeration is a complete proof only over finite subject matter (like truth tables). Infinite domains need proof techniques.

questions.question: Scheduling exams so no student has two at once is, structurally, a problem about…
options: coloring the vertices of a conflict graph
questions.explanation: Courses are vertices, conflicts are edges, and time slots are colors — this is graph coloring, covered in Phase 05.

questions.question: How many pairs (A, B) of subsets of an n-element set satisfy A ⊆ B?
questions.explanation: Each element is in neither, in B only, or in both — 3 independent choices per element, so 3ⁿ. The lesson's code verifies this.
